draft.title: Growth and development compared
card: a change in size, such as getting taller or heavier. It can be measured, for example in centimetres or kilograms.
a change in ability and complexity, such as learning to walk, speak or handle strong feelings. It is harder to measure than size.
Development happens in four areas: physical, social, emotional and intellectual. Physical development is a change in how the body works and what it can do.
The two often happen together, but they are not the same thing. A person can grow in size without developing a new ability, and can develop a new skill without growing.
draft.remember: Growth is getting bigger. Development is getting more able and more complex.

a.q: Which of these is an example of development rather than growth?
opts: A toddler learns to join two words into a sentence
A toddler gains two kilograms over six months
A toddler is five centimetres taller than last year
A toddler's feet grow two shoe sizes in a year
a.why: Joining words into a sentence is a new ability, so it is development, in this case intellectual. The other three are changes in size that can be measured, which is growth.
a.clue: Which change is about what the child can do, not how big they are?

b.q: Priya is 15. Over one year she grows 8 cm taller. In the same year she learns to calm herself before exams and to cope better when friends argue. What is the best description of this year?
opts: Growth in height and emotional development
Growth in height and intellectual growth
Development in height and emotional growth
Development in height and social growth
b.why: Gaining 8 cm is a change in size, so it is growth. Calming herself and coping with arguments are new abilities in handling feelings, so they are emotional development. The tempting options swap the words growth and development, but size is growth and ability is development.
b.clue: Sort each change into size or ability, then name the area of the ability.

a.best: A toddler learns to join two words into a sentence

b.best: Growth in height and emotional development
